- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00 or ≤ 0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is trending down.
- Model frequently overshoots in the first 5–7 days of forecast horizon after a spike; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 1–2% per day post-spike.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is > 10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast slightly to match sentiment direction.
- Model underperforms when sentiment is high but price is consolidating — reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.
- Forecast horizon 1–7 days: model tends to lag sentiment shifts; align forecast with sentiment direction within 2–3 days of change.
- Forecast horizon 8–30 days: model often overreacts to short-term sentiment; apply smoothing filter to dampen volatility.
